implementation_notes: C++ sprawl is frequently a per-class gRPC or REST endpoint: a 'user service' that returns a user, a 'validation service' that validates, an 'order service' that stores orders. Each is a separate binary with its own deployment, its own health check and its own version, and the whole business operation now crosses a network boundary several times. The C++-specific cost is that each binary is statically or dynamically linked, so N services means N copies of the runtime and N security-update surfaces. The detection is the build and deploy configuration plus the binary count; the consolidation is to put them in one binary with clear internal boundaries until a real isolation or scaling reason appears.
idiom_name: one binary per capability; gRPC service per class
pitfalls: N statically-linked binaries means N copies of the runtime and N CVE surfaces for the same library version.
Splitting at the class boundary rather than at a business-capability boundary, which is the C++ form of bounded contexts mistaken for service boundaries.
A network hop inside a transaction that used to be a function call, adding a partial-failure mode to code that had none.
